title: Closed-ball density limits give the same open-ball density limit
statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let ν be any Borel measure on ℝ^P, x ∈ ℝ^P and θ ∈ [0, ∞]. Write ω_n = unitBallVolume n (the Lebesgue measure of the unit ball of ℝ^n) and, for ρ > 0, c(ρ) = ω_n·ρ^n ∈ [0, ∞], with ρ^n entered via ENNReal.ofReal. If ν(B̄_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → θ in [0, ∞] as ρ ↓ 0, then ν(B_ρ(x))/c(ρ) → θ as ρ ↓ 0. Here B̄_ρ(x) and B_ρ(x) are the closed and open balls, and quotients are taken in [0, ∞].
lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (θ : ℝ≥0∞), Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => ν (closedBall x ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 θ) → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => ν (ball x ρ) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 θ)
